BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                               OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI


    In the Matter of the Request of Evergy        )
    Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy Missouri Metro for   )                 Case No. ER-2026-0143
    Authority to Implement a General Rate         )
    Increase for Electric Service                 )



                               MECG Response to Commission’s Order
                       Shortening Time to Object to Stipulation and Agreements

          COMES NOW, the Midwest Energy Consumers Group, (“MECG”) and pursuant to 20

CSR 4240-2.115, the Commission’s Order Shortening Time to Object to Stipulation and

Agreements issued October 5, 2026, and the Commission’s Order Shortening Time to Object to

Stipulation and Agreement issued October 7, 2026, states its positions on the following non-

unanimous stipulations as follows:

1)        Programs Stipulation and Agreement filed on Oct. 7, 2026.1

          MECG does not object.

2)        LLPS Partial Stipulation and Agreement (Public) filed on Oct. 5, 2026.2

          MECG understands that the Staff has filed an objection to this stipulation and it is now a

joint position of the signatories.3 To the extent it is necessary to preserve its ability to take a

position on these issues within its post-hearing briefs based on the testimony and evidence at

hearing MECG objects to this stipulation.

3)        Non-Unanimous Partial Settlement – Rate Design filed on Oct. 5, 2026.4

           MECG is a signatory to this stipulation and urges the Commission to adopt its terms as an

appropriate resolution of the issues addressed within.

4)        Partial Stipulation and Agreement - Non-C&I Rate Design filed on Oct. 2, 2026.5

          MECG does not object.

5)        Partial Stipulation and Agreement filed on Oct. 2, 2026.6

          MECG does not object to the terms, except with respect to the Depreciation provisions

insofar as the issue of the plant life adjustments recommended by Mr. Brian Andrews are reserved

for hearing. As the document notes: “MECG does not oppose the agreement except that Brian

Andrew’s life estimate adjustments are preserved for hearing. This preserves issue 17 (A) in part

for MECG at hearing. A determination on that issue could impact the rates and the Staff revenue

requirements in this Agreement.”

          Specifically, MECG argues the depreciation rates used should take into account the

probable retirement dates of generating units. When selecting probable retirement dates, all

reliable sources of information should be considered. Here, EMM’s 2026 IRP Annual Update was

filed in May 2026 and identifies that EMM now plans to continue operating several EMM

generation units for at least an additional five years beyond its current estimates—moving from

2040 to at least 2045. EMM’s depreciation study in the rate case utilized 2040 as the probable

retirement dates for Iatan Unit 1 and La Cygne Unit 2. MECG maintains the Commission should

require the depreciation expense and rates in this case to take into account the updated probable

retirement dates for Iatan Unit 1 and La Cygne Unit 2. For clarity, at this time, MECG is not

pursuing its license extension adjustment for Wolf Creek.
